note: mapping_basis=data_labels. DERIVATION is core model s3 pattern 1: data/spain_2014_family.do infixes DA3032 at the ES3032 DATA LIST positions (P1201..P1210 = cols 118-127, identical to ES3032 lines 10-11 and to the questionnaire's column codes (118)-(127)) under lower-cased names, and Bookmark 7 sets item = the variable name (p1201..p1210; lower-casing is Stata naming) -- nothing positional, so Step 5b is exempt and no verification_/verify_ files were written. LABELS vs QUESTIONNAIRE: ES3032 VARIABLE LABELS P1201-P1210 were compared with the P.12 rows of cues3032.pdf read from a 300-dpi render of scanned page 4 (not OCR); the questionnaire's hyphenated line breaks ('ma-/nera', 'pare-/jas', 'vivien-/da', 'perso-/nas', 'so-/lución', 'hi-/jo/a') are rejoined, and 'aco/ger' on the P1208 row (a line break whose hyphen is not visible in the scan, the 'o' underlined) is rejoined as 'acoger', which is also the label's spelling. 8/10 agree character for character. TWO DIFFER, and item_text follows the QUESTIONNAIRE (the wording the interviewer read aloud) rather than the label: P1208 questionnaire 'Un hombre o una mujer solos pueden adoptar...' vs label 'Un hombre o una mujer solo/a pueden adoptar...'; P1210 questionnaire '...criar igual de bien a un hijo/a que...' vs label '...a un/a hijo/a que...'. Both are gender-inflection variants of the same sentence and neither bears on which code is which item -- the label still pins each code to its row, and the questionnaire's column code does so independently. The other eight item_text values are the variable labels verbatim (checked in build.R). Items 3, 4, 6 and 9 are noun phrases ('Las parejas que deciden no convivir en la misma vivienda', 'El matrimonio entre personas del mismo sexo', ...) rated on the same agreement scale; that is how the questionnaire prints them and they ship unexpanded. VALUE LABELS identical on all 10: 1 'Muy de acuerdo' 2 'Bastante de acuerdo' 3 '(NO LEER) Ni de acuerdo ni en desacuerdo' 4 'Poco de acuerdo' 5 'Nada de acuerdo' 8 'N.S.' 9 'N.C.' -- matching the questionnaire's printed list. RESP BY DESIGN: the .do recodes 3 (the volunteered, not-read-out midpoint), 8 and 9 to missing, so live resp is {1,2,4,5} and option rows ship for those four codes only; there is no resp 3 row, and resp keeps its gap (4 = Poco de acuerdo, not the third option). Dropped by the .do, per item p1201..p1210: code 3 = 80/167/316/274/222/223/236/245/130/227 (2120 total); code 8 = 67/28/149/54/79/60/92/87/46/71 (733); code 9 = 5/5/26/17/16/18/12/11/13/12 (135). DA3032 carries no code 0 and no other codes on cols 118-127, so P.12 was asked of all 2464 respondents (it follows the 'A TODAS LAS PERSONAS ENTREVISTADAS' header before P.9 with no new filter); 11 respondents gave 3/8/9 on all ten items and have no rows, which is why live has 2453 ids. CHECKED, decisive: reading DA3032 (2464 records, all 385 bytes; id = row number) at cols 118-127, dropping 3/8/9 as the .do does, with cov_sex col 254 and cov_age cols 255-256 (99 -> NA), reproduces the live table exactly: 21652 rows both, 2453 ids both, 0 only-live / 0 only-rebuilt rows, 0 resp and 0 cov_age mismatches; cov_sex stored as the Stata value label (Hombre 10624 rows, Mujer 11028, no cross cells). Live item x resp (1/2/4/5): p1201 1320/776/147/69, p1202 135/282/613/1234, p1203 441/692/441/399, p1204 770/799/246/304, p1205 956/933/172/86, p1206 884/1034/164/81, p1207 748/717/323/336, p1208 788/970/227/136, p1209 1109/1061/73/32, p1210 777/922/320/135 -- every item uses all four levels; 'to have children couples should be married' (p1202) is the only item the sample rejects (mean 4.1) while mixed couples (p1209) and equal rights for unmarried couples (p1201) are the most endorsed (1.6), coherent with the content. validate_items.R --table-sets passed (10 items, resp {1,2,4,5}). TEXT (text_source=study_materials): instructions = the P.12 stem verbatim from cues3032.pdf ('A continuación voy a leerle ...'), shared by all ten rows, so instructions not section_prompt, one trivial section; the '(NO LEER)' marker belongs to the dropped option 3 and is not shipped. translation_source=machine_translation: CIS publishes Estudio 3032 in Spanish only; the _translated columns are English written by this project, option translations aligned with the siblings (Strongly agree / Quite agree / Slightly agree / Do not agree at all) -- issues-page line owed at upload. RIGHTS: instrument_rights_register.csv CIS row (verdict allow, 2026-09-22, every CIS survey year) applied, not re-derived. Not an instrument-name mismatch: the dictionary description (unmarried couples' rights, marriage before children, living apart together, same-sex marriage, divorce, childless couples, adoption by homosexual and single people, mixed couples, single parenting) names the ten P.12 rows in order. Not confused with sibling _matrimony (Bookmark 6, P.10) or _adoption (P.17), different question blocks.
public_note: The neutral midpoint (volunteered, not read out) was recoded to missing, so resp takes 1, 2, 4, 5 (strongly agree .. do not agree at all) with no 3; items p1208 and p1210 follow the questionnaire's wording, which differs from the CIS variable labels only in gender inflection ('solos' vs 'solo/a', 'un hijo/a' vs 'un/a hijo/a'); item text English is IRW machine translation of the Spanish-only CIS questionnaire
